privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Strena is a wishlist app for family and friends. This page explains what it stores about you, why, who else is involved, and how to have it deleted.

sections.heading: Who runs Strena
body: Strena is run by Federico Lunardon, a private individual in the United Kingdom, who is responsible for your data. For any question or request about your data, write to infostrena@proton.me.

sections.heading: What Strena stores
body: Your account: your email address, the name you show to others, your language and look settings, and when you joined.
Your lists and items: what you add to them, such as names, links, descriptions, prices, ratings and pictures.

Sharing and gifts: the email addresses you share lists with, and which items people reserve as gifts. The owner of a list never sees reservations; other people the list is shared with see who reserved an item, so the same gift isn't bought twice.

Signing in: sign-in codes and links are stored only in scrambled form and expire after 10 minutes. Each device you sign in on is remembered with a name (such as the phone's model) until you sign out of it. The app keeps your sign-in in the phone's secure storage; the website keeps it in your browser's storage. Strena uses no cookies.
Notifications: if you allow them, your phone's push notification address. When an item you reserved changes, a short note of the change is kept until you have been told, and deleted a day later.
Server logs: the web server records the IP address, the time and the page of each request, to keep the service running and secure. Logs are deleted after 14 days.

sections.heading: How it is used
body: Only to run Strena for you: to sign you in, show your lists to the people you share them with, and send you sign-in codes and notifications. There are no ads, no analytics or tracking, and your data is never sold or used for profiling.
Under UK data protection law, this processing is necessary to provide the service you asked for, and, for the server logs, in the legitimate interest of keeping it secure.

sections.heading: Who else handles it
body: Mailjet (in the EU) sends Strena's emails, so it receives your email address and the message.
If you allow push notifications, Expo (in the US) and Google's Firebase Cloud Messaging deliver them, so they receive your phone's push address and the notification text.
When you add an item from a link, the Strena server visits that page to fill in the details. The shop sees the server's address, not yours.

sections.heading: Where it is kept, and for how long
body: Your data is kept on Strena's server in the United Kingdom, until you delete it or your account. Backup copies are kept for up to 14 days.
Deleting your account (in Settings) removes your account, lists, items, pictures, shares, reservations and signed-in devices straight away. Backup copies disappear within 14 days.

sections.heading: Your rights
body: You can ask for a copy of your data, have it corrected or deleted, or object to how it is used, by writing to infostrena@proton.me. You can also complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ico.org.uk) or the data protection authority where you live.

sections.heading: Children
body: Strena is not meant for children under 13.

sections.heading: Changes
body: If this policy changes, this page is updated and the date at the top changes with it.
